privacy.metaDescription: Wanderlust's privacy posture: what we collect, which vendors we use, and how to reach us. Draft pending final legal review.
privacy.headline: What we collect and how we handle it
privacy.draftBannerBody: This page describes Wanderlust's current data practices but has not yet been reviewed by counsel. A finalized policy will be published before public launch. In the meantime, the facts below are accurate to how the app operates today.
privacy.intro: Wanderlust is designed to collect as little as it can and reuse what it must. This page describes what we actually store, which vendors we rely on, and how to reach us if you have questions or want your data removed.

dataItems.title: Account information
dataItems.body: Your email address (for sign-in) and optional display name. Birth year if you provided one during sign-up (used to confirm you're at least 13, then stored).

dataItems.title: Authentication data
dataItems.body: Encrypted session tokens and, if you enabled them, passkeys / one-time codes / two-factor-authentication secrets. Managed by Better Auth. We never store plaintext passwords.

dataItems.title: Learning progress
dataItems.body: Which courses you enrolled in, which lessons you've started or completed, and where you last left off. Used to let you resume across devices.

dataItems.title: Purchase records
dataItems.body: If you buy a paid course, Stripe processes the payment. We store a Stripe purchase ID and your enrollment, not your card number. Stripe's policy governs card handling.

dataItems.title: Media you upload (creators only)
dataItems.body: If you're a creator, files you upload are stored in Cloudinary under your account context. Creators retain full rights to their source media.

dataItems.title: Support conversations
dataItems.body: If you open a support thread, the messages you write and any files you attach are stored so we can respond. You can request deletion.

dataItems.title: What we do not collect
dataItems.body: We do not run third-party advertising trackers. We do not sell your data. We do not build a profile of you across apps. The only cross-site fetches are to our own vendors listed below.

dataItems.title: Hunt progress and location
dataItems.body: If you play a hunt, we store which stops you opened and when, against a random token your browser generates. That token is not an account and is not linked to you. Location is different: when a hunt stop opens by you arriving somewhere, your device's position is read and compared to that place ON YOUR DEVICE ONLY. Your latitude and longitude are never sent to us and are never stored — there is no field in our database that could hold them. We only learn that a stop opened.

privacy.vendorsIntro: Each of these vendors processes data on our behalf. They're selected for security posture and documented in our infrastructure notes.

vendors.name: Neon (Postgres)
vendors.role: Primary database. Hosted in AWS us-east region.

vendors.name: Cloudinary
vendors.role: Media storage and delivery: 360° photos, 360° video, images, audio.

vendors.name: Better Auth
vendors.role: Authentication framework (runs against our own Neon database).

privacy.rightsBody: You can request a copy of the data we hold about you, corrections to incorrect data, or deletion of your account and associated data. Open a support thread and we will respond within a reasonable timeframe. For users in the EU/EEA, UK, or California, statutory rights apply and will be detailed in the finalized policy.

terms.metaDescription: Wanderlust's terms of service: how accounts work, content rights, payments, and changes. Draft pending final legal review.
terms.headline: Terms of service
terms.draftBannerBody: These terms describe the current rules for using Wanderlust but have not yet been reviewed by counsel. A finalized version will be published before public launch. In the meantime, the points below are accurate to how the service operates today.
terms.intro: Using Wanderlust means agreeing to a few reasonable things. We've kept them short because no one reads twelve-thousand-word terms documents. The full legal version is coming; these are the plain-language commitments in the interim.
useItems: Use Wanderlust for its intended purpose: learning from place-based courses and, if you're a creator, publishing them.
Don't abuse the service: no scraping at scale, no attempts to circumvent authentication, no load-testing our endpoints without permission.
Don't upload content you don't have the rights to, and don't upload content that is illegal where you or the viewer is located.
Report bugs and abuse through the support channel; don't exploit them.
terms.accountsBody: You must be at least 13 years old to create a Wanderlust account. You're responsible for keeping your sign-in methods secure. You can close your account at any time by contacting support; doing so revokes your access and deletes your personal data on a reasonable schedule.
terms.contentBody: If you're a creator, you retain all rights to the 360° media, text, and other content you upload. You grant Wanderlust a license to host, transcode, and deliver that content to learners you've chosen to reach. We never claim ownership. If you close your account, your published courses are unpublished.
terms.paymentsBody: Paid courses are processed via Stripe. A receipt is emailed on purchase. For refund requests, open a support thread within a reasonable window of purchase; we'll respond case by case. The finalized terms will specify the refund window and conditions.
terms.changesBody: We'll update these terms before public launch and when material changes happen afterward. Active users will be notified by email when that occurs. For questions, open a support thread.

accessibility.metaDescription: How Wanderlust treats accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA commitments, what we enforce at publish, what we're still improving, and how to report an issue.
accessibility.headline: Built to be usable. And we mean it.
accessibility.intro: Wanderlust is designed for WCAG 2.1 AA. Accessibility is a launch requirement, not a nice-to-have. This page is our public statement about what that means in practice, what we enforce before any course goes live, and where we're still improving.

commitments.title: Keyboard-operable, every interactive element
commitments.body: Every button, link, form field, and 360° viewer control is reachable and usable with the keyboard alone. Every interactive element has a visible focus ring.

commitments.title: Transcripts on every video
commitments.body: A transcript is required on every video before the course it sits in can be published. Enforced by the publish gate, not the honor system. Learners who don't hear can follow along; learners who want to read can read.

commitments.title: 2D fallback on every 360° asset
commitments.body: Every 360° photo and every 360° video has a 2D still-frame fallback so learners on assistive tech, low-bandwidth connections, or devices without WebGL still get the content.

commitments.title: Screen-reader verified before every public push
commitments.body: VoiceOver on iOS and macOS plus TalkBack on Android are run against the learner flows before any public staging deploy.

commitments.title: Color contrast and reduced motion
commitments.body: Body text meets a 4.5:1 contrast ratio; large text and UI meet 3:1. We respect the prefers-reduced-motion OS setting: no auto-rotation, no autoplay, no long transitions if you've asked for less motion.

commitments.title: Mobile-first at 320 px up
commitments.body: The learner experience is designed to work on the smallest commonly-used phone and scale up. No 'best viewed on desktop.'

commitments.title: Automated tests on every change
commitments.body: Our continuous-integration pipeline runs axe-playwright and pa11y-ci on the public pages on every pull request. Regressions on these pages block merge.

accessibility.gapsBody: We're not perfect. The immersive 360° viewer has its own keyboard + focus story we rely on the upstream library for and continue to harden. Audio descriptions for course video are on the roadmap but not yet enforced by the publish gate. We ship improvements in small branches and track regressions against this public commitment.
accessibility.reportBody: If a page, course, or feature isn't usable for you (for any reason, on any device), please tell us. Open a support thread and we'll prioritize it. Accessibility bugs are not feature requests.

meta.title: Wanderlust: Learn by standing inside a place
meta.description: A place-based learning platform where every lesson begins with standing inside a real location, captured through 360° photo, 360° video, and drone footage.

landing.headline: Every lesson starts by standing inside a real place.
landing.subhead: Rainforest canopies. Museum galleries. Coral reefs. Chocolate workshops in Mexico City. Captured in 360° and taught through curriculum built on top of the footage.
landing.featureImmersiveBody: Every course is built around a real location captured in 360° photo, 360° video, and drone footage. Not a plugin. The center of the product.
landing.featureCreatorBody: One person with a camera, a drone, and a laptop can publish a full multi-media course. Creators keep full rights to their footage.
landing.featureLearnerBody: Resume across devices, download for offline use, and take courses keyboard-only or with a screen reader. WCAG 2.1 AA from day one.
landing.flagshipDescription: A walk through Mexico City's chocolate museum, tracing cacao from Olmec origins to modern bean-to-bar craft. Launching in English and Spanish.
landing.globeSectionTitle: See every tour on a globe
landing.globeSectionBody: Spin the Earth to find the real places creators have mapped — then step inside. Pick a pin or a tour from the list and the globe flies you there.

howItWorks.metaDescription: How a Wanderlust course works: for learners, for creators, for museums and universities. Place-based learning with no AI-generated content.
howItWorks.headline: Stand inside a real place. Learn from the people who know it.
howItWorks.subhead: Every course is anchored to a location captured in 360°. Then a curriculum is built on top of the footage. No stock photos. No AI-generated text. No voice you don't recognize.

learnerSteps.title: Find a place you want to stand inside
learnerSteps.body: Browse courses by destination. Every course is anchored to a real place: a museum hall, a trail, a workshop, a reef. What you see in the preview is what you'll stand inside.

learnerSteps.title: Enroll in one click
learnerSteps.body: Free courses: one click and you're in. Paid courses: one Stripe checkout and you're in. Either way, your enrollment tracks across every device you sign into.

learnerSteps.title: Take lessons one block at a time
learnerSteps.body: Each lesson is a short stack of blocks: a passage of text, a 360° photo you can turn inside, a video, a caption. Keyboard-only works. Screen reader works. WCAG 2.1 AA from day one.

learnerSteps.title: Never lose your place
learnerSteps.body: A strip under every tour lists each stop, marks the one you are in, and ticks off the ones you have seen. It counts honestly — "Stop 3 of 9, 6 left" is the real number of scenes, never padded. Tap any stop to jump straight there, so a room with no exit arrow can never strand you. Getting lost is the most common reason people abandon a virtual tour; this is the fix.

learnerSteps.title: Travel between tours
learnerSteps.body: Some places connect. Inside a tour you might see an arrow that opens a preview card for a different tour by a different creator — name, cover, a sentence of context. You decide whether to step through. Creators opt in on both ends; there's no surprise navigation.

learnerSteps.title: Find tours on a spinning globe
learnerSteps.body: Open the Tours page and the world turns: a 3D globe with a pin on every place we've mapped, color-coded by type — hikes, museums, concerts, and more. Spin it, pick a pin or a tour from the list, and step inside. You can pull the globe up from inside any tour too, to see what else is nearby. The full list of tours stays right beside it for keyboard and screen-reader browsing.

learnerSteps.title: Pick up where you left off
learnerSteps.body: Close the tab on your laptop, open it on your phone. Your last lesson is marked, and the course card says 'Resume where you left off.' Manage your profile, password, active sessions, and cross-tour preferences from your account page anytime.

learnerSteps.title: Send it to someone
learnerSteps.body: Finished a tour worth sharing? One button hands it to your phone's share sheet or copies the link. Where the creator has marked the high point of their tour, the link opens there — so whoever you send it to arrives at the view worth travelling for, not at the front door.

creatorSteps.title: Capture the place
creatorSteps.body: Shoot 360° photos and video with a consumer camera. A single Insta360 + a drone + a laptop is enough to publish a full multi-media course.

creatorSteps.title: Upload to your library
creatorSteps.body: Drag files straight into Wanderlust. They go to Cloudinary via signed upload (nothing ever hits our server). Name them, tag them, attach a transcript to any video before you publish.

creatorSteps.title: Bring in video you already have
creatorSteps.body: Already have footage on YouTube? Paste a link to add a YouTube block to any lesson, or set a YouTube video on a destination to publish it as a video tour — it plays in a privacy-friendly player, and the destination still appears on the globe.

creatorSteps.title: Build destinations and scenes
creatorSteps.body: A destination is a real place. A scene is one vantage point inside it: one 360° photo or video. Build as many scenes per destination as you need, swap in new footage anytime. Back from a shoot with twenty files? Assign them to the tour, then create every scene in one step instead of filling in the form twenty times.

creatorSteps.title: Tune the visitor view
creatorSteps.body: Pick the scene visitors land on first. Rotate the horizon if a panorama leans. Swap the default scene-link arrow for your own SVG. Set a portrait card image so your destination reads cleanly in narrow listings. Every choice is per-destination — your other tours stay exactly as you set them. You can also set which way visitors face as they arrive from each specific scene, so walking a corridor in either direction feels like walking rather than being spun around.

creatorSteps.title: Mark the high point
creatorSteps.body: Every tour has one view worth travelling for. Name it, and it becomes what a shared link opens to and what the preview image shows when someone pastes that link into a chat. You can also sequence your scenes, so the stop list follows the order you meant rather than the order you happened to upload in. Both are optional — leave them alone and the tour behaves exactly as it does now.

creatorSteps.title: Link to nearby places (or don't)
creatorSteps.body: Connect a hotspot in your tour to another creator's destination, or set a 'next tour' CTA at the end. Linking is off by default. Both you and the destination you point to must opt in; visitors see a preview card before being sent anywhere. Inside a course, the target opens in a new tab so course progress isn't lost.

creatorSteps.title: Assemble lessons from blocks
creatorSteps.body: Pick a block type (text in Markdown, a 360° photo, a standard video, a 360° video) and compose a lesson. Reorder, edit, delete. Learners see the block order you set.

creatorSteps.title: Publish when it's ready
creatorSteps.body: Set a price (or free), pick a default language, flip the status to published. Paid courses route through Stripe Checkout automatically. The app creates the Stripe Product and Price for you on first purchase.

commitments.title: No AI-generated content
commitments.body: No AI-written lesson text, no AI-fabricated voices, no AI-generated imagery. Every word and frame comes from a human who stood in that place. This is the explicit differentiator.

commitments.title: Accessibility is a launch gate
commitments.body: WCAG 2.1 AA compliance before a course can go public. Transcripts required on every video. 2D fallback required for every 360° asset. Screen-reader smoke tests before every staging push.

commitments.title: Mobile-first from 320 px up
commitments.body: The learner player works on an iPhone SE as well as a 27-inch desktop. No squishing. No 'best viewed on desktop' caveats. Performance budget is enforced at 150 KB gzip above the fold.

commitments.title: Creators keep their footage
commitments.body: Upload to Cloudinary under your account context. Creators retain full rights to the source media. Wanderlust never claims ownership of your 360° captures.

commitments.title: We close the loop on bug reports
commitments.body: When you report something broken in support chat, we resolve it and ask you to confirm. If it's still broken, one tap flips the thread back to us with priority bumped. If it worked, we close the loop. The satisfaction figure below is the live aggregate over the last 90 days — never a marketing target.

commitments.title: You opt in, not out
commitments.body: Cross-tour links are off by default. Both the creator linking and the destination being linked must turn it on. Visitors get a preview card before any cross-tour navigation. No commercial relay, no engagement loops, no surprise hops.

howItWorks.partnersBody: Wanderlust is built to partner. The flagship course is a real collaboration with MUCHO Museo del Chocolate in Mexico City. Museums get a dignified way to publish digital tours without a Unity budget. Universities get an ADA-compliant, human-taught alternative to slide decks. If you run an institution and want to explore a partnership, reach out through the support channel after signing in.

howItWorks.ctaBody: Start with the free MUCHO course. Or sign up and publish your own.
